chunks: He said: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn reported to me, he said: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umayr, from more than one source, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"Cursed by God are the people of analogy (qiyas), for they have changed the word of God and the tradition of His Messenger (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) and they have accused the truthful ones of lying about the religion of God, the Mighty and Majestic."

key_terms.الصادقين: The truthful ones - referring to the Imams and reliable transmitters of the faith
key_terms.القياس: Qiyas - analogical reasoning, a method of legal deduction rejected by the Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia view on qiyas (analogical reasoning) in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) condemns the proponents of qiyas (analogical reasoning in jurisprudence), declaring them cursed by God. This statement was made in the context of early Islamic legal debates where some jurists, particularly the Ahl al-Ra'y school in Iraq, relied heavily on qiyas to derive religious rulings. The Imam charges them with three transgressions: distorting God's word, altering the Prophet's practice, and falsely accusing the truthful transmitters of the faith.
